best_for: Windows users and admins with a full drive who want to see, as colored blocks, which folders and files eat the space, on anything from a laptop to a file server.

points.title: See where the space went
points.text: WinDirStat scans a drive or folder and draws it as a treemap, where each file is a block sized by how much space it takes. Big, forgotten files stand out at a glance, so you know what to delete first.

points.title: Version 2 does much more
points.text: The 2.x releases add sunburst and flame-graph views, a duplicate finder, scans of network shares, phones over MTP and cloud storage such as S3, Azure Blob and WebDAV, plus CSV and JSON reports and dark mode.

points.title: Old Windows still works
points.text: The project supports Windows 7 through 11 and Windows Server 2008 R2 through 2025. The MSI installers listed here cover x86, x64 and Arm64, and all install for every user on the machine.

points.title: Faster scans need admin rights
points.text: Elevating the app gives quicker scans of local NTFS drives, and the deleted-file recovery tool needs administrator access too. Without it, scans still work, just slower.

points.title: Duplicate checks can guess
points.text: Duplicate search compares file contents by hash. With sparse hashing on, it only samples files and labels matches as probable, so check before you delete.

points.title: Free and portable
points.text: WinDirStat is free under the GPL version 3 or later. A zip build runs without installing; turn on portable mode in settings to keep its settings beside the program. The Windows listing keeps 14 versions.
